concept.title: What is DITA?

conbody.p: Darwin Information Typing Architecture (DITA) is an XML-based standard for modular, topic-oriented content authoring and publishing. Developed originally by IBM and now maintained by OASIS, DITA has become the industry standard for technical documentation in enterprises worldwide.

XML (Extensible Markup Language) provides the foundation for DITA. As a structured, text-based markup language, XML stores, organizes, and transports data in a way that is both human-readable and machine-readable. DITA authoring uses XML tags to enable structured reuse, conditional publishing, multi-channel delivery, and AI optimization.
